title: Leading his own band at the La Vida, 1936
summary: Howard led the band at La Vida in 1936 with Jim Robinson and Paul Barnes, and they discuss Barnes on saxophone.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well who else did you play with in the 20s?

Well mostly I used to always have my own band, you see. I played at the La Vida, well Jim was in charge, Jim Robinson was in charge, but I was the leader and so forth of that group. And at the Pallet Theater, well that was my group.
When were you at the La Vida? 36.
36 I was there. That's the first time it's the audition of the Social Security cards, I'll never forget that. Yeah, I got the card there in 36.
Who did you have in the band there? You had Jim as well.
Yeah, well Jim, Paul Barnes, Sidney Flusia played the guitar, Benny Turner played the piano, Robert Davis played the drum. It was six of us. That's what they said.
What did you say? You had clarinet or saxophone? Saxophone, Paul. Did he play clarinet at that time?
Yeah he could play but he didn't play the clarinet over there. He just played the saxophone.
I just wonder, because you know on the old records you hear him mostly on saxophone in the 20s?
Well yeah, when he recorded with the Pops where he played nothing but the sax.
You mean Papa Celeste? Yeah, that's right. And Jelly Roll too I think the same thing.
Yeah, when he was with Joe Oliver. He played the saxophone. I see.

Yeah so he would be more famous as a saxophone player then I guess. That's right, he would. The way you say it and everything it looks like. You must have played with somebody else in the 20s, or you say you had some other places, you had your own band.
